description.content: It is inefficient to create and manage a large list of DOM elements within a scrolling container if only a few of those elements are visible. The primary purpose of this component is to improve performance by only rendering the DOM nodes that a user is able to see based on their current scroll position.
This component renders a virtualized list of elements with either fixed or dynamic heights.
Responsible for rendering a group of cells given their index ranges.

This is an advanced property. It is useful for situations where the Grid requires additional, overlayed UI (such as a Gantt chart or a calendar application). The easiest way to override it is to decorate defaultCellRangeRenderer.
Defaults to defaultCellRangeRenderer.
Additional props (eg onWheel) to spread onto the outer Grid element.

description.content: Vertical scroll offset to initially render (and scroll to) the Grid at. Only the initial value is used: changing this prop later has no effect (use scrollToPosition to scroll). This also works with server rendering: the cells at this offset are rendered on the server, and they stay in place when the page is hydrated. Ignored if a scrollElement is specified (which then determines the vertical offset).

Prevents re-rendering of visible cells on scroll end. (Opts out of the isScrolling param passed to cellRangeRenderer, to avoid the extra render when scroll stops.) Visible cells are still re-rendered when the Grid's props change or forceUpdate() is called.

description.content: Responsible for calculating the number of rows to overscan before and after a specified range. By default (accessibilityOverscanIndicesGetter), at least one row is overscanned in each direction (for accessibility). See Grid overscanIndicesGetter for details.
Number of rows to render above/below the visible bounds of the list. This can help reduce flickering during scrolling on certain browsers/devices.
Note that this property has performance implications: the higher the value, the more work needs to be done in reaction to each scroll event.

description.content: Number of rows in list.

Either a fixed row height (number) or a function that returns the height of a row given its index: ({ index: number }): number. If function is used, specify estimatedRowSize for more consistent scrolling behavior.
Responsible for rendering a row given its index. It receives index, isScrolling, isVisible, key, parent, and style parameters.
The style parameter specifies how the row is to be sized and positioned and must be passed through to the rendered row element. The key parameter must also be applied to the rendered element.
Element that scrolls the List (instead of the List scrolling itself): "window", or a scrollable DOM element (e.g. a container that the List is rendered within, along with other content).

The List then renders at its full height, renders only the rows visible within the scroll element's viewport, and its scroll methods scroll the scroll element. Its position within the scroll element is measured when the scroll element scrolls or is resized, and when the List re-renders (e.g. call forceUpdateGrid() if content above the List changes size without the List re-rendering). Pass null while the scroll element isn't available yet (e.g. before a ref to it has been attached); the List then renders the rows at its top.
